text:
Sam Rivera: Legal ping: tenant T-77 ended up writing to ap-southeast despite tenant policy set to local-only. Proxy fell back to nearest region when control-plane consent info wasn't present. We need a safer default than blind fallback.

Linnea Park: Can you drop the proxy log? Curious whether it was a full cache miss or a control-plane delay.

Sam Rivera: Sanitized log snippet:
```
[2026-03-19T03:14:02Z] proxy=decision tenant=T-77 req=xyz999 cp_consent=null prefer_hint=ap-southeast -> fallback=route-nearest status=proxy-forwarded
[2026-03-19T03:14:02Z] proxy=write target=ap-southeast store=accept id=store-7a
```

Omar Haddad: Two thoughts: (A) make proxies authoritative for final decision by seeding them earlier (pre-warm), or (B) change runtime fallback to "hold" instead of forward. Pre-warm = push consent snapshots to edge via our control-plane stream.

Diego Flores: "Hold" semantics look promising: when consent undefined, proxy returns a short-term 202-hold (or an HTTP 202 with header) and writes the payload to a local quarantined queue that is not visible to downstream services until consent arrives. Then background reconciler either commits to tenant-region or deletes after TTL. This avoids illegal cross-region writes.

Linnea Park: What does the client see in hold mode? We should avoid confusing API clients. Proposal: return 202 with a Retry-After and a location to poll for status. Also set X-Redwood-Write-Status: held;hold-id=<uuid>. Example response:
```http
HTTP/1.1 202 Accepted
X-Redwood-Write-Status: held;hold-id=111e4f
Retry-After: 8
Content-Type: application/json
{ "status":"held","hold_id":"111e4f","expected_retry_seconds":8 }
```
Clients can either poll the status endpoint or register a webhook to be notified if/when the write is committed.

Omar Haddad: Implementation sketch for pre-warm + hold fallback:
- control-plane publishes consent snapshot per-tenant to edge-sync stream (compact topic).
- proxies consume the compact topic and maintain a small cache keyed by tenant_id -> consent_hash, allowed_regions, timestamp. Cache TTL is e.g., 60s and updates are idempotent.
- On request: if cache has consent -> route accordingly. If cache missing OR consent explicitly denies region -> apply fallback policy: hold | quarantine | forward depending on tenant policy.
- Offer global default: hold for 15s then fall back to quarantine if still unresolved.

Diego Flores: Quarantined queue contract: local, encrypted, mark for legal review, auto-retry task that will commit when consent becomes available, and a metrics endpoint for queue depth. Quarantine records should include original_request_id, tenant_id, payload_checksum, and hold_reason.

Linnea Park: Risks: 1) increased tail latency for writes if we hold; 2) possible durability concerns for local quarantine stores; 3) canary/model routing bias if region pinning is used. We need mitigations: bounded hold window, persistent local queue with replication to local region storage, and an override flag for model-routing when pinned by experiments.

Omar Haddad: Canary interactions: model-serving needs to know if region pinning is advisory vs authoritative. If we treat pre-warmed consent as advisory, model routing will still be balanced; but for legal-sensitive tenants treat consent as authoritative which will exclude them from canaries automatically. We'll need a per-tenant flag in the consent snapshot: canary_opt_out=true|false.

Sam Rivera: Telemetry we should add immediately: consent_push_lag_ms, consent_cache_miss_rate, hold_rate_per_tenant, quarantine_commit_rate, hold_expiry_count, write_status_poll_latency. Dashboards for legal team and infra.

Diego Flores: Test plan ideas:
- chaos test: drop edge-sync updates for 30s and assert proxy returns 202-held not forwarded.
- integration: seed consent snapshot with canary_opt_out and assert model-routing excludes tenant.
- durability: simulate disk pressure on local quarantine store and verify alerting.

infra-bot: infra-bot: FYI rolling proxy canary v3 with local-quarantine support scheduled for 2026-03-21T01:00:00Z UTC.

Linnea Park: Action items: I'll draft a short design note with header spec and state machine for proxy decisions (cache-hit -> route, missing -> hold -> quarantine -> final fallback). Diego 1 will draft the quarantine-store contract and retention/rotation rules. Omar will instrument canary flags in consent feed. Sam will coordinate legal sign-off and add required dashboards.

Sam Rivera: One more operational detail: add an admin endpoint to force-release held writes for emergency ops with audit trail. That will satisfy SRE and legal for escalations.

Omar Haddad: I'll follow up with a small PoC that pushes compact consent updates and measure median push lag. If we see >200ms we'll increase cache TTL and tune backoff.

Sam Rivera: Good plan. Let's keep the rollout conservative: enable hold-mode for EU and AP tiers first, monitor quarantined queue, then expand. I'll open the PR for the RFC tonight.
